title: Oath and Wolf
premise: Yara Montrose carves bones into keepsakes that whisper the memories of their dead owners, a gift she has kept secret since her mother's execution for the same 'witchcraft.' When a dying courier presses a wolf-skin map into her hands, Yara discovers it is half of an ancient covenant binding the human realm of Thornfell to the wolf-kindred beyond the mountains — and her own bloodline was meant to be its keeper. Hunted by the king's bone-priests who murdered her mother, Yara crosses Thornfell with Fen, a wolf-kindred exile who despises humans, to find the covenant's second half before the winter solstice, when the broken oath will unleash a famine that devours both realms. At the covenant stone, Yara learns her mother died refusing to sacrifice herself to renew it; instead, Yara rewrites the oath itself, binding the realms through shared memory rather than blood, at the cost of surrendering her own cherished memories of her mother. The book ends with the covenant renewed, Yara unable to remember why she weeps when she touches carved bone, but free — and with Fen choosing to stay in the human world as her memory-keeper.
about_author: Astrid Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archaeologist who spent a decade cataloguing burial goods in northern mountain ranges before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy steeped in folklore about borders, bargains, and the things we inherit without asking.

chapters.title: The Courier's Last Breath
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In her workshop above the smuggler town of Greymoss, Yara finishes a commission when a wounded stranger staggers in, pursued by the king's bone-priests, and dies pressing a wolf-skin map fragment into her hands — a map that speaks her name. The bone-priests arrive searching for it, forcing Yara to flee with nothing but her tools. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant inheritance; the past she buried has found her.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with interludes from Fen's. Fleeing through the Thornfell passes she knows better than anyone, Yara is ambushed by Fen, a wolf-kindred exile sent to retrieve the map. Forced into uneasy alliance, they discover the map only reveals its path when touched by bone that carries memory — and Yara's mother's keepsake pendant is the key. Emotional beat: grudging trust forming as grief becomes navigation.

chapters.title: The Stone That Hungers
chapters.summary: Fen's POV opening, shifting to Yara's. Reaching the covenant stone on solstice eve, they find the bone-priests waiting, led by High Carver Vess — who reveals Yara's mother refused the blood sacrifice and that the covenant demands a life freely given. Betrayed by a smuggler ally sold to the priests, Yara is captured; Fen must choose between his exile and her. Emotional beat: despair and revelation — every inheritance is also a debt.

chapters.title: Oath Rewritten
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the solstice altar, Yara refuses both sacrifice and refusal: using her carving gift, she cuts a new covenant into the stone, binding the realms through exchanged memory instead of spilled blood, paying with her memories of her mother. The famine breaks; Vess's order shatters as the truth of their murders surfaces. Fen stays beside her, carrying what she gave away. Emotional beat: bittersweet transcendence — identity remade, love remembered by proxy.
